title: Tell me you eat fish: gharial
storyboard: Film: creator does the 'tell me without telling me' trend, miming a long snout with both arms

scenes.headline: Tell me you only eat fish without telling me
*long, skinny snout full of interlocking teeth*
Males grow a pot-shaped 'ghara' on the snout tip
scenes.body: Named after the Indian ghara pot, it works as a vocal resonator for a loud buzz and helps attract females.

scenes.headline: Critically Endangered
scenes.body: The gharial population fell by 58% between 1997 and 2006, from habitat loss, fishing pressure and hunting.

caption:
That snout is a fishing tool.

Adult gharials primarily eat fish, while juveniles also take insects, crustaceans and frogs. The opening photo is a wild female in Bardiya National Park, Nepal.

Source: Smithsonian's National Zoo (Gharial).  Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
